assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the first controlled, non-perturbative framework that treats Mott localisation, local moments and coherent quasiparticles on equal footing, and combined with electronic-structure methods (DFT+DMFT) it has become a working tool for real correlated materials. Original, conceptually clean (the infinite-dimension limit and the self-consistent impurity mapping), and with very broad impact on transition-metal oxides, heavy fermions, f-electron systems and magnetism.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt's infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar's mapping onto a self-consistent impurity problem, and the earlier Müller-Hartmann and Brandt-Mielsch contributions form the core. Within the supplied names, Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt are a natural trio, though Metzner (not on the list) is an unresolved omission and Kotliar's DFT+DMFT and Georges' later development blur the boundary between the foundational and applied parts.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of use, many independent implementations and a stable interpretation, with quantitative successes for materials such as the iron pnictides, nickelates and f-electron systems. Recognition is timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Metzner is not among the credited names, so a fully fair allocation of the foundational credit may be impossible within this list.
Quantitative accuracy for long-range correlations and low dimensions is limited, and the DFT+DMFT double-counting problem is not fully settled.
I work in neighbouring electronic-structure theory and should discount any familiarity bias; this is my own assessment from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of quantum matter defined by bulk topology and protected boundary states. The Kane-Mele Z2 quantum spin Hall proposal, followed by the HgTe-based prediction and the Molenkamp-group observation of edge transport, give a clean chain from idea to experiment. The impact spans materials theory, band-structure calculation and spintronics.
assessment.attribution: The theory (Kane and Mele) and the first experimental realisation of the quantum spin Hall state (Molenkamp, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal) are well matched in this trio. However, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the 3D topological insulator work of Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, and Hasan, are not all represented, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation in many materials, strong first-principles support for band inversion, and a stable interpretation. The prize is timely, although the field's credit history is crowded.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and for 3D topological insulators (Hasan, Moore, Balents, Fu) is not captured by the supplied names.
Quantisation in the quantum spin Hall edge is less clean than in quantum Hall systems.
B012 overlaps this candidate and a fair configuration might merge the two.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and, above all, the giant TMR in epitaxial and sputtered MgO junctions turned spin-dependent tunnelling into the read-head and MRAM technology of today. The MgO result rests on a spin-filtering mechanism (symmetry-dependent evanescent states) first understood through first-principles calculation, which is a striking example of electronic-structure theory predicting a device effect.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki (room-temperature TMR), and Parkin and Yuasa (MgO-based giant TMR, reported independently in 2004) are the experimental core; Butler's first-principles prediction of coherent tunnelling is decisive for understanding and could arguably displace one experimentalist. The 1975 Julliere and Moodera results are outside the supplied names, and the GMR prize of 2007 already covers adjacent ground.
assessment.maturity: Technologically mature and independently reproduced; the physics is stable. Recognition is timely, with some risk that it is seen as an extension of the 2007 spintronics prize.
uncertainties: Whether Butler's theory should be included instead of one of the experimental names is unresolved.
Priority between the Parkin and Yuasa groups was contemporaneous and the technology-driven character may weigh against a physics prize.
Moodera and Julliere are not among the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions are topologically protected spin textures that arise from the interplay of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, exchange and anisotropy. Real-space and reciprocal-space observation, electric-current manipulation at very low densities, and their application proposals make this a central achievement in modern magnetism, and one that atomistic spin simulations and first-principles calculations have helped interpret.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer (neutron-scattering discovery of the skyrmion lattice in MnSi), Tokura (real-space Lorentz imaging and multiferroic skyrmions) and Wiesendanger (atomic-scale skyrmion lattice and writing/deleting at a surface) are plausible as a trio. Theory by Bogdanov and by Rößler, Bogdanov and Pfleiderer, and the first observation by Mühlbauer et al., complicate the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independent confirmations across materials classes, though practical racetrack-memory applications remain unproven, and some interpretations (for example skyrmion Hall effects and pinning) are still developing.
uncertainties: Bogdanov's theoretical priority, which predates the observations, is not among the credited names.
Application impact is still prospective, so maturity for a prize is somewhat lower than for DMFT or TMR.
Division between Pfleiderer's group and the Mühlbauer et al. author list is not fully resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The spin Hall and inverse spin Hall effects convert between charge and spin currents through spin-orbit coupling and underpin much of modern spintronics, including spin-orbit-torque switching and spin-pumping detection. The theory, the optical observation in semiconductors and the electrical detection in metals form a coherent and widely used toolkit.
assessment.attribution: Dyakonov and Perel predicted the effect in 1971, Awschalom's group provided the first optical observation (2004), Jungwirth the contemporaneous observation in a hole system and Saitoh the inverse spin Hall detection of spin pumping. With four credited names and a limit of three, the choice among Awschalom, Jungwirth and Saitoh is difficult, and Hirsch's revival of the idea and Sinova's intrinsic mechanism are outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, including in first-principles Berry-curvature calculations of intrinsic contributions. Recognition is timely, but the credit is diffuse.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Jungwirth and of Hirsch, Sinova, Zhang and others is a substantive attribution problem.
The discovery is a family of related effects with separate decisive experiments, so recognition may need to split the parts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted flat bands at the magic angle, and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moiré engineering as a new platform for strongly correlated physics. A genuine and rapidly generative new direction where electronic-structure modelling and experiment meet.
assessment.attribution: A fair prize configuration exists in theory (Bistritzer and MacDonald) plus the decisive experiment (Jarillo-Herrero, with Yuan Cao as first author). Other experiments (Dean, Young, Yazdani, and others) and the earlier theory of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto are not included.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories, but the nature of the superconductivity, the correlated states and the role of strain and disorder are still debated. Recognition may be somewhat premature compared with the established topics above.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram remain unsettled.
Earlier theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) and other experimental groups raise unresolved credit questions.
Reproducibility of device-to-device behaviour is a known concern.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model and is an extraordinary instrumental and collaborative achievement. The theoretical prediction was recognised in 2013, but the discovery experiments themselves were not.
assessment.attribution: The Nobel statutes allow at most three laureates, while the discovery was made by thousands of people. The spokespersons and the proponents of the detector concepts are plausible representatives, but the choice is inherently arbitrary and perhaps unfair to the many who contributed to the analyses and detectors.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by two independent experiments with decade-long coupling measurements. Recognition is clearly mature, apart from the attribution problem.
uncertainties: No supplied configuration can fairly capture a collaboration of this size.
The 2013 prize already recognised the Higgs mechanism, which could reduce the urgency.
Outside my own field, so my assessment of the relative contributions of individuals is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Angle-resolved photoemission on the cuprates mapped the Fermi surface, the d-wave gap, the pseudogap and the nodal and antinodal quasiparticle structure, which gave direct spectral evidence on the electronic structure of high-temperature superconductors. It transformed ARPES into a quantitative tool for correlated electrons, which I regard as central to understanding why spectra look the way they do.
assessment.attribution: Campuzano, Shen and Takahashi lead the experimental programmes, but the technique's development involved many groups (including Dessau, Hüfner and others), and the field's key interpretations were collective. The credit for instrument development and for specific cuprate results is not neatly separable.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, though the pairing mechanism the spectra were meant to clarify is still unsettled, which reduces how conclusive the discovery is.
uncertainties: The technique is a measurement method and not a single discovery; prize framing is difficult.
Credit among the many ARPES groups is diffuse, and the omitted names are substantial.
The central problem of cuprate superconductivity remains unresolved.
